growing_specifications.description: High-value medicinal and culinary climbing vine famous for its crisp, bitter green fruit containing charantin and polypeptide-p. It is a staple commercial crop across the Philippines (Pinakbet, Ginisang Ampalaya) cultivated with bamboo trellises.

category_why.title: Why is Bitter Gourd classified under Cucurbit / Vine?
category_why.summary: Ampalaya belongs to the botanical family Cucurbitaceae (gourd family). It exhibits distinct vining morphology with climbing tendrils and monoecious flowers that require trellis management.
points: Climbing Habit & Tendrils: The plant develops slender herbaceous vines with auxiliary tendrils that grasp supports, elevating foliage and fruit off wet ground to prevent fungal decay and soil-borne pests.

Monoecious Flowering Biology: Separate male (staminate) and female (pistillate) yellow flowers bloom on the same vine, requiring insect pollinators (such as honeybees) for successful fertilization and fruit development.

Pepo Fruit Classification: Produces a specialized berry with a thick, ribbed, and warty exterior rind containing charantin and momordicin, the bioactive compounds responsible for its signature therapeutic bitterness.

harvest_why.title: Why is the harvest maturity set to 55 days?
harvest_why.summary: Commercial harvesting at 50–55 days from transplanting captures peak fruit crispness, optimal market size, and prevents fruit over-ripening and seed hardening.
points: Germination & Seedling Phase (Days 1–16): Seeds emerge in 5–7 days, followed by true leaf expansion and transplanting readiness.
Vegetative Trellis Climbing (Days 17–34): Rapid branch elongation, lateral shoot pruning, and trellis canopy establishment.
Anthesis to Fruit Maturation (Days 35–55): Female flowers bloom and develop into market-ready gourds within 15–20 days after pollination.
Risk of Over-Ripening (>60 Days): Delayed harvesting causes fruits to turn yellow-orange, develop fibrous spongy flesh, and split open, making them unmarketable.

watering_why.title: Why does Bitter Gourd need watering every 2 days?
watering_why.summary: Ampalaya possesses a shallow fibrous root system and broad foliage with high transpiration rates during rapid fruit cell expansion.
points: Critical Fruit Expansion: Developing fruits contain over 92% water. Inconsistent irrigation during fruit enlargement causes stunted, twisted, or excessively bitter gourds.
Moisture Stress Prevention: Letting soil dry out for 3 or more days induces blossom and fruitlet abortion, reducing overall harvest yields.
Root Aeration & Disease Control: Daily waterlogging suffocates roots and invites Phytophthora root rot and damping-off. A 2-day furrow or drip cycle maintains optimal 60–70% field moisture capacity.

soil_why.title: Why does Bitter Gourd require pH 6.0–6.7 and Well-Draining Loam?
soil_why.summary: A slightly acidic to neutral root zone maximizes essential phosphorus, magnesium, and trace mineral uptake needed for heavy continuous flowering.
points: Maximum Nutrient Uptake: In the pH 6.0–6.7 range, phosphorus and potassium are most bioavailable, stimulating vigorous root branching and continuous blossom setting.
Drainage & Compost Integration: Loam or sandy loam enriched with decomposed organic manure retains moisture without standing water, safeguarding roots from waterborne pathogens.

varieties.disease_resistance: High tolerance to Papaya Ringspot Virus - Cucurbit Strain (PRSV-W) and Leaf Spot
varieties.description: Deep green extra-long hybrid bitter gourd developed by East-West Seed. Features thick, prominent ridges, high fruit firmness, and excellent post-harvest shelf life for long-distance transport.

varieties.disease_resistance: Strong tolerance to Downy Mildew and Anthracnose
varieties.description: Premium commercial hybrid cultivar renowned for heavy prolific fruit setting, uniform cylindrical shape, and glossy dark green skin favored by wet-season commercial growers.

varieties.disease_resistance: Moderate tolerance to Bacterial Wilt and Gummy Stem Blight
varieties.description: Intermediate-light green hybrid with blunt, smooth ridges and tender flesh. Preferred by urban restaurants and home cooks for its gentle bitterness and rapid 52-day turnaround.

varieties.disease_resistance: High natural hardiness against local insect pests and environmental stress
varieties.description: Traditional open-pollinated heirloom variety from Pampanga and Ilocos. Characterized by pointed, short tapered fruits with intense bitterness and distinctive aroma prized for authentic Ilocano Pinakbet.

varieties.disease_resistance: Tolerant to high heat and intermittent drought
varieties.description: Short, stout ovoid bitter gourd popular in Visayas and Mindanao. Quick to mature (48 days) with thick juicy walls ideal for stuffing with ground pork or quick egg stir-fries.

varieties.disease_resistance: Specially bred for Bacterial Wilt and Cucurbit Virus Resistance
varieties.description: Public-sector scientific hybrid developed by the Institute of Plant Breeding (IPB - UPLB). High yielding with strong field endurance in wet-season tropical conditions.
